tagline: One of the Bosphorus's most beautiful villages — Ottoman wooden mansions, boutique restaurants, and an unhurried pace that feels far from the city's chaos.

items.name: Arnavutköy İskelesi Café
items.description: Right on the ferry landing with classic Bosphorus views. Simple Turkish breakfast, tea, and coffee in a timeless setting.
items.tip: The weekend breakfast spread is excellent. Come early for a window table.

items.name: Kışlık Café
items.description: A neighbourhood café tucked into one of Arnavutköy's charming side streets. Good coffee, low-key atmosphere, local regulars.

items.name: Poseidon Restaurant
items.description: One of Istanbul's most celebrated fish restaurants, right on the Bosphorus. Exceptional fresh fish and a stunning view. Book well ahead.
items.tip: Request a table on the waterfront deck. The whole sea bass is outstanding.

items.name: Tarihi Arnavutköy Balıkçısı
items.description: A simple, beloved fish restaurant in the heart of the village. No frills, great fish, very local crowd.
items.tip: Ask for the catch of the day — it changes daily and is always the best choice.

items.name: Sunset Grill & Bar
items.description: Upscale international restaurant with panoramic Bosphorus views. More of a special occasion restaurant — worth it for the setting.
items.address: Adnan Saygun Cad., Ülker Parkı, Ulus

items.name: Bosphorus Waterfront Walk
items.description: A beautiful coastal walk along the Bosphorus between Arnavutköy and Bebek. Ottoman yalıs (waterfront mansions) line the route.

items.name: Yıldız Parkı (Upper)
items.description: The forested park above the neighbourhood has walking paths, Ottoman pavilions, and sweeping views of the Bosphorus.

items.name: Antique & Art Shops
items.description: Arnavutköy's main street has a string of small antique shops and art galleries. Great for browsing on a slow afternoon.

tips: Arnavutköy is best reached by bus from Beşiktaş (25E or 22 lines) or a pleasant 25-min waterfront walk.
The neighbourhood is very small — everything worth seeing is within a 10-minute walk.
Avoid driving on weekends — parking is essentially impossible along the main street.
The best time to visit is a weekday morning when it genuinely feels like a Bosphorus village.
